source_tier: Third-party GitHub mirror exact AEC-named June 16 2025 generated CSV header, primary catalogue verifies named files, no authenticated AEC download or first_public_at
source_prior: McGinn & Maruyama Economic Record 2025 already documented causal effect candidates→informal in earlier periods; AEC 2025 review independently documented contemporary relation but case-selected on high informality. Our analysis confirms association, NOT novel science or replicated causal design.
restrictions: No individual/party scoring, not actually a prospective frozen evaluation, ChatRelay off, no main merge.
A: Does pre-election nomination count improve out-of-state 2025 descriptive prediction of informal percentage over pre-election close-roll enrolment and AEC geography class?

C.execution: Executed deterministic leave-one-state-out over 8 complete Australian state/territory groups, 150 division rows. Predictors baseline training mean, OLS log(close-of-rolls) + AEC demographic one-hot (train-only categories), and same plus nomination count. No state fixed effect for an unseen state, no post-vote turnout, no post-vote informal swing and no outcome as input. Aggregated held-out MAE and RMSE weighted by division.

F: Declared H1 supported for this internal geographical CV and 2025 public outcomes. While feature definitions available before poll, the source files generated after election and analysis run posthoc; NOT live forecast at dated cutoff. Only eight state clusters and geographic/demographic changes limit generalization.
G: Source same institution one 2025 election; article by McGinn & Maruyama 2025 is prior causal literature but not a replication of their identification design
I: Only electoral division-level measurement, no profiling
J: Stop line per R5 until genuinely new future outcome (or original authentic historical 2022–2025 change); maintain T024 Codex for original bytes and full suite.
